newsitem.title: UK: Euro insurers don't exploit single market - industry.
newsitem.headline: Euro insurers don't exploit single market - industry.

text.p: European insurers are failing to take advantage of the single market to sell their products across national borders, an industry conference was told on Thursday.

Giorgio Casagrande, chairman of the EU standing committee of the Bureau International de Producteurs d'Assurances et de Reassurances, told delegates at the Insurance 96 conference in London that the third life and nonlife insurance directives passed by the European Union in the early 1990s should have meant consumers would have access to a wide choice of products from more than 2000 insurers based all over the region.
"One would have imagined an explosion of cross border activities after transcription of the directives into national legislations. In reality, very little has followed, he said.
Casagrande said the current situation was little changed from the way it was before the advent of the single market.
"Insurers seem to be happy to carry on, operating in their own home market or, in the case of a few, using their long established subsidiaries or agencies in the European union.
"One could well conclude that insurers are, for various reasons, unwilling to be forced by demand to operate in a wide open competitive market."

Casagrande said the reasons for the inertia among insurers included language problems, a lack of knowledge and experience in the different markets, and the difficulty of training staff to operate outside traditional borders.
He said that the European Commission had now recognised that unless a new regulation was passed allowing insurance brokers the same cross-market, the single insurance market would remain crippled.
He added that the European financial services commissioner had asked to be kept fully informed about the problem.
